layout_details.content: ## 3 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 3.1 Scope of this document
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: This document describes the tagging of IEC/ISO standards-type documents in XML. It gives recommendations for the harmonized tagging of content in the IEC/ISO environment and can be used for the following purposes:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - as a basis for IEC/ISO members for their conversion and production process
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - to help conversion providers set up the conversion from unstructured content to XML according to the NISO Standards Tag Suite (NISO STS)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: This document applies to NISO STS 1.0 (October 2017). Versions of this document refer to the implementation status at IEC and ISO, not to NISO STS versions.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 3.2 Coding Guidance
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NISO STS is based on ANSI/NISO Z39.96 (JATS) and is backwards compatible with ISO STS.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: It provides a common XML format that developers, publishers, and distributors of standards, including national standards bodies, regional and international standards bodies, and standards development organizations, can use to publish and exchange full-text content and metadata of standards.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The full description as well as supporting materials can be found at https://www.niso-sts.org/. Elements and attributes are described in more depth at https://www.niso-sts.org/TagLibrary/niso-sts- TL-1-0-html/index.html.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Structures are provided to encode both the normative and non-normative content of standards, adoptions of standards, and standards-like documents that are produced by standards organizations.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ISO/IEC standards should be drafted according to the ISO/IEC Directives "Rules for the structure and drafting of International Standards", in their current edition. Because the directives have changed over time and may not have always been followed faithfully, past standards may have been coded differently, for instance, a clause described as required may be absent from an older standard, and other such deviations from the latest directives may exist.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Going forward, these past standards should not be used as reference or precedence for exotic coding.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Tagging to be used only where required in legacy standards will be marked as "Legacy tagging".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Cases where tagging is under investigation for optimisation will be marked as "Under investigation for future implementation".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 3.3 Tagging differences between ISO and IEC
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ISO and IEC strive to use identical tagging wherever contents are identical. For those cases where contents or usages are different, the ISO variant is highlighted in red, the IEC one in blue.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
ISO variant ...
IEC variant ...
layout_details.label: table

layout_details.content: A recurring difference is that of IDs - where ISO is using underscores in IDs, IEC is using dashes. For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
ISO @id="sec_foreword"
IEC @id="sec_foreword"
layout_details.label: table

layout_details.content: An online standards development tool is currently being developed at ISO and IEC. In this context arbitrary unique IDs will be assigned and managed by the tool. Editorial notes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Where comments on the structure of standards (e.g. from the ISO/IEC Directives, Part 2) or other background information is provided in addition to coding instructions, it will be preceded by the words "Editorial note" and set in a light grey box, like this:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
Editorial note
...
layout_details.label: table

layout_details.content: ## 3.4 Formatting of elements and attributes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Throughout the text, XML elements are written in angle brackets and formatted in bold, attributes are prefixed by @ and formatted in italics, as illustrated below:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## <element>
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: @attribute
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 3.5 Multilingual documents
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For multilingual documents, @xml:lang should be used on the most outer block level element. For example, if a document has alternating sections in English and French, then it is sufficient to provide the @xml:lang="en" or @xml:lang="fr" in the top level <sec> element only.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 4 Structure
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 4.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A standard or standards-type document is divided into three parts:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: front matter
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: body
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: back matter
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The complete document should be coded within the root <standard>. For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```xml

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>

<standard xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:tbx="urn:iso:std:iso:30042:ed-1"

xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">

    <front>

        <std-meta>

            <title-wrap xml:lang="en">

                <intro>...</intro>

                <main>...</main>

                <compl>...</compl>

                <full>...</full>

            </title-wrap>

            <title-wrap xml:lang="fr">

                <intro>...</intro>

                <main>...</main>

                <compl>...</compl>

                <full>...</full>

            </title-wrap>

            <proj-id>...</proj-id>

            <std-ident>

                <originator>ISO</originator>

                <doc-type>IS</doc-type>

                <doc-number>9512</doc-number>

                <part-number/>

                <edition>3</edition>

                <version>1</version>

            </std-ident>

            <std-org std-org-type="sdo">

                <std-org-abbrev>ISO</std-org-abbrev>

            </std-org>

            <content-language>en</content-language>

            <std-ref type="dated">ISO/DIS 9512</std-ref>

            <std-ref type="undated">ISO/DIS 9512</std-ref>

            <doc-ref>ISO/DIS 9512(en)</doc-ref>

            <release-date>2018-08-06</release-date>

            <meta-date type="vote-start">2018-08-06</meta-date>

            <meta-date type="vote-end">2018-10-29</meta-date>

            <comm-ref>ISO/TC 126/SC 1</comm-ref>

            <secretariat>AFNOR</secretariat>

            <ics>65.160</ics>

            <page-count count="18"/>

            <std-xref type="revises">

                <std-ref>ISO 9512:2002</std-ref>

            </std-xref>

            <permissions>

                <copyright-statement>All rights reserved</copyright-statement>

                <copyright-year>2018</copyright-year>

                <copyright-holder>ISO</copyright-holder>

            </permissions>

            <self-uri>...</self-uri>

            <custom-meta-group>

                <custom-meta>

                    <meta-name>special-voting-rule</meta-name>

                    <meta-value>NO FDIS BALLOT</meta-value>

                </custom-meta>

                <custom-meta>

                    <meta-name>price-ref-pages</meta-name>

                    <meta-value>18</meta-value>

                </custom-meta>

                <custom-meta>

                    <meta-name>generation-date</meta-name>

                    <meta-value>2018-06-08 07:42:48</meta-value>

                </custom-meta>

            </custom-meta-group>

        </iso-meta>

```

layout_details.content: The following front and back matter content are not captured in the XML:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - cover pages
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - table of contents
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - page headers and footers containing the name of the document, page numbers etc.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - index if it refers to page numbers (if coded, indexes refer to marked-up elements)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 4.2 Front matter
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 4.2.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: <front> is required in ISO/IEC standards and can comprise the following front matter:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - standards organizations metadata
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - other optional national metadata
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - an introduction
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - a foreword
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The front matter of a standard may contain:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - document-level metadata (<std-doc-meta>)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - standards organization metadata (in one or more of the elements <std-meta>, <iso-meta>, <regmeta>, or <nat-meta>)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - prose material such as notes and sections, particularly as used for placeholder elements not yet articulated in NISO STS (for example, patents or particular copyright statements) or for older content with different structures
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 4.2.2 Metadata
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
ISO Legacy tagging ISO-specific metadata about the document in legacy content. For NISO STS implementation going forward, this will be std-meta.
IEC std-meta contains IEC-specific metadata about the document.
layout_details.label: table

layout_details.content: No organization metadata should be captured within <std-doc-meta>. Instead, <std-meta>, <iso meta>, <reg-meta>, or <nat-meta> should be used as appropriate, with relevant titles, copyright statements, dates, etc. Organization-specific metadata in <std-meta> will override relevant data in <std-doc-meta>. This element allows for accurate capture of standards organizations' data when publishing or adopting standards.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: To capture the copyright information for the current document in the metadata, use the <permissions> element. For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```xml

<std-meta>

...

    <permissions>

        <copyright-statement>All rights reserved</copyright-statement>

        <copyright-year>2011</copyright-year>

        <copyright-holder>ISO</copyright-holder>

    </permissions>

</std-meta>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For multiple copyrights, ISO and IEC use different coding:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 4.2.3 Foreword
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Editorial note
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The foreword is generally required and unnumbered and should contain no tables or graphics.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: This is the first titled clause. It is coded as <sec>. For a more detailed description of <sec> in general, see 4.3.2.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Attributes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: @sec-type="foreword"
layout_details.label: text
text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Foreword
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ISO (the International Organization for Standardization) is a worldwide federation of national standards bodies (ISO member bodies). The work of preparing International Standards is normally carried out through ISO technical committees. Each member body interested in a subject for which a technical committee has been established has the right to be represented on that committee. International organizations, governmental and non-governmental, in liaison with ISO, also take part in the work. ISO collaborates closely with the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) on all matters of electrotechnical standardization.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: should be coded as
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: <sec id="sec_foreword" sec-type="foreword">
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 4.2.4 Introduction
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Editorial note
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: If present, the introduction should follow the foreword and is generally not numbered. In certain cases, introductions can contain subclauses, which will then be numbered "0.1/0.2" etc.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The introduction is coded as <sec>. For a more detailed description of <sec> in general, see 4.3.2.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Attributes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: @sec-type="intro"
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ISO
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - unnumbered introduction: @id="sec_intro"
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - numbered introduction: @id="sec_0"
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - subclauses of the introduction: @id="sec_0.1"
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) Unnumbered introduction with no subclauses:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Introduction
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The Quality management principles underlying the ISO 9000 family of standards (of which the ISO 10000 series form a part) emphasize the importance of human resource management and the need for appropriate training. They recognize that customers are likely to both respect and value an organization's commitment to its human resources and its ability to demonstrate the strategy used to improve the competence of its personnel.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Personnel at all levels should be trained to meet the organization's commitment to supply products of a required quality in a rapidly changing market place where customer requirements and expectations are increasing continuously.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: should be coded as:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
Introduction

The Quality management principles underlying the ISO 9000 family of standards (of which the ISO 10000 series form a part) emphasize the importance of human resource management and the need for appropriate training. They recognize that customers are likely to both respect and value an organization's commitment to its human resources and its ability to demonstrate the strategy used to improve the competence of its personnel.

Personnel at all levels should be trained to meet the organization's commitment to supply products of a required quality in a rapidly changing market place where customer requirements and expectations are increasing continuously.

layout_details.content: ## 4.3.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The main textual portion of a standards document is usually captured in the <body> tag. The <body> is required in ISO/IEC documents.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: It contains multiple clauses and subclauses (henceforth both will be referred to as "clauses" in this document, unless the differentiation is important). Clauses must be captured in <sec>, usually starting with clause 1 (normally "Scope"), followed by other sequentially and hierarchically numbered clauses.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example: clauses 1.2.1 and 1.2.2 are within clause 1.2, which is within clause 1.

Part 1:General requirements
1 Scope
This part of ISO 2631 defines methods for the measurement of periodic, random and transient whole-body vibration. It indicates the principal factors that combine to determine the degree to which a vibration exposure will be acceptable. Informative annexes indicate current opinion and provide guidance on the possible effects of vibration on health, comfort and perception and motion sickness. The frequency range considered is0.5Hz to80Hz for health, comfort and perception,and0.1Hz to0.5Hz for motion sickness.
Although the potential effects on human performance are not covered, most of the guidance on whole-body vibration measurement also applies to this area. This part of ISO 2631 also defines the principles of preferred methods of mounting transducers for determining human exposure. It does not apply to the evaluation of extreme-magnitude single shocks such as occur in vehicle accidents.
This part of ISO 2631 is applicable to motions transmitted to the human body as a whole through the supporting surfaces: the feet of a standing person, the buttocks, back and feet of a seated person or the supporting area of a recumbent person. This type of vibration is found in vehicles, in machinery, in buildings and in the vicinity of working machinery.
